question: Does the exact 3.1.175 release expose the NSH mw/exec and runtime primitives required by the custom ET_REL bootstrap?

nsh_exec.behavior: Parses a hexadecimal callable, prints Calling %p, then invokes it through BLX; the entry tolerates the print callback return value in r0.

nsh_mw.behavior: Parses address[=value] and optional count, performs four-byte writes or reads, and has no cache maintenance.

mpu.configure_contract: Rejects region > 7, length <= 0x1f, unaligned base, and unsupported access attributes; publishes RBAR/RLAR and requires DSB/ISB before transfer.

sram_text.publication: The exact firmware startup protects the copied SRAM text range; custom executable allocations use the recovered MPU helpers and DSB/ISB.

control_flow_evidence: The exec handler calls the parsed address with BLX and does not retain the image.
The mw handler writes four-byte words and performs no instruction synchronization.
The bootstrap must restore the cave and clear RLAR before releasing a temporary MPU region.
The exact firmware contains no verified stock insmod/rmmod loader boundary for this path.
unsafe_assumptions: All findings are static IDA evidence; no device execution was performed.
The resident stage-2 loader must assume ownership of allocations and MPU regions before stage 1 returns.
